description: The departure board your data already has. Bind a table and it flips in, character by character, like the split-flap board in a 1970s station. Then it pages itself on the wall screen, lights a lamp beside every status and, when the data refreshes, flips only the characters that changed. Real split-flap mechanics Every character sits on its own drum that only turns forward, so a change walks through the characters in between and the board settles in a cascade: sweep, curtain, row by row, scattered or all at once, at the speed you choose. Only what changed flips. A data refresh turns just the characters that moved; resizing or switching the theme never re-flips the board. Digit drums for times and numbers, and accented letters (Č, Ř, Ö, Ł, É and more) added right next to their letter when your data uses them. Write {green}, {red} or {yellow} in the text for a solid colour flap. Your data, in columns Time, destination or item, up to six detail columns, up to six number columns and a status column, each bound to a field. Numbers are never cut short. Every column has its heading, width, alignment and visibility in the format pane, listed by the field's own name. Status words become On track, Watch, Problem or Done from word lists you can edit, with English, Czech, German, French, Spanish and Polish built in. The word stays on the board and each class lights a lamp of its own shape,…
